Recent Developments 2026 Activity Increase in Repurchase Program Authorization On February 18, 2026, our board of directors approved an increase in authorization under our existing repurchase program from $750 million to $1.75 billion, excluding excise tax. As of February 20, 2026, approximately $1.2 billion remains available for future repurchases under our repurchase program, excluding excise tax. Cash Dividends On February 18, 2026, our board of directors approved (i) an increase to our annual base dividend to $1.52 per share of Class A Common Stock beginning with the dividend payable for the fourth quarter of 2025, and (ii) a combined quarterly base and variable cash dividend of $0.52 per share of Class A Common Stock and $0.65 per OpCo Unit payable on March 12, 2026. Divestiture of Non-Permian Assets On February 9, 2026, we completed the Non-Permian Divestiture for net cash proceeds of approximately $617 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. The divested properties consisted of approximately 9,400 net royalty acres in the Denver-Julesburg, Eagle Ford and Williston basins with current production of approximately 4,750 BO/d. Proceeds from the Non-Permian Divestiture were used to repay the Term Loan (as defined below) and to reduce borrowings outstanding on the 2025 Revolving Credit Facility (as defined below). 2025 Activity Acquisitions Update Sitio Acquisition On August 19, 2025, we completed the Sitio Acquisition in an all-equity transaction valued at approximately $4.0 billion, including customary transaction costs and post-closing adjustments and the partial retirement of Sitio’s net debt of approximately $1.2 billion. The mineral and royalty interests acquired in the Sitio Acquisition represent approximately 25,300 net royalty acres in the Permian Basin and approximately 9,000 net royalty acres in the Denver-Julesburg, Eagle Ford and Williston basins, for total acreage of approximately 34,300 net royalty acres. 29 Table of Contents 2025 Drop Down On May 1, 2025, we completed the 2025 Drop Down for consideration consisting of (i) $873 million in cash including customary post-closing adjustments, and (ii) the issuance of 69,626,640 OpCo Units and an equivalent number of shares of our Class B Common Stock (collectively, the “Drop Down Equity Issuance”). Financial Statements and Supplementary Data of this report. At December 31, 2025, we had a net asset derivative position related to our commodity price derivative contracts of $21 million. Utilizing actual derivative contractual volumes under our contracts as of December 31, 2025, a 10% increase in forward curves associated with the underlying commodity would have increased the net asset position by $5 million to approximately $26 million, and a 10% decrease in forward curves associated with the underlying commodity would have 42 Table of Contents increased the net asset position by $2 million to approximately $23 million. However, any cash derivative gain or loss may be substantially offset by a decrease or increase, respectively, in the actual sales value of prod uction covered by the derivative instrument. Credit Risk We are subject to risk resulting from the concentration of royalty income in producing oil and natural gas properties and receivables with a limited number of several significant operators who sell our production to numerous purchasers. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, two operators each accounted for more than 10% of our income, respectively. For the year ended December 31, 2023, one operator accounted for more than 10% of our income. See Note 2— Summary of Significant Accounting Policies in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data of this report for further details. Each of our operators sell to multiple purchasers. We do not require collateral and the failure or inability of our significant purchasers to meet their obligations to us due to their liquidity issues, bankruptcy, insolvency or liquidation may adversely affect our financial results. Volatility in the commodity pricing environment and macroeconomic conditions may enhance the credit risk from our operators and purchasers. Interest Rate Risk We are subject to market risk exposure related to changes in interest rates on our indebtedness under the 2025 Revolving Credit Facility and the Term Loan. The terms of the 2025 Revolving Credit Facility provide for interest on borrowings at a floating rate equal to term SOFR or an alternate base rate (which is equal to the greatest of the prime rate, the federal funds effective rate plus 0.50% and 1-month term SOFR plus 1.0%, subject to a 1.0% floor), in each case, plus the applicable margin. The applicable margin ranges from 0.125% to 1.000% per annum in the case of the alternate base rate loans and from 1.125% to 2.000% per annum in the case of term SOFR loans, in each case, based on the pricing level. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers the declared dividend more than threefold, so the base distribution is funded from internally generated cash rather than borrowings, a meaningful cushion for a royalty business with no capital spending obligation.

The current ratio sits well above the sector median, reflecting a liquid working-capital position against modest near-term liabilities; this supports short-dated obligations even though the ratio is flattered by a low current-liability base.

key_risks.text: Royalty income is concentrated: two operators each contributed more than a tenth of income, and the issuer takes no collateral from purchasers, so an operator insolvency or payment failure would hit cash flow directly without offsetting security.

Borrowings under the revolving facility and term loan float at term SOFR plus a margin, leaving interest cost exposed to rate resets; the term loan was repaid only after year-end from divestiture proceeds, so refinancing and rate risk persist into the current period.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income is negative while cash interest paid remains substantial, so the reported interest coverage ratio is negative and sits far below the sector median; earnings-based debt service is therefore not demonstrated and cash flow must carry the burden.

Cash flow to debt is below the sector median but above the next risk-band boundary, leaving limited headroom; a modest decline in operating cash flow would push the ratio toward the lower tier, so distribution policy and commodity prices warrant close monitoring.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is modest, anchored by strong cash conversion and a liquid balance sheet, but leverage cannot be assessed because depreciation and capital spending are not disclosed in the bundle, leaving gross and net leverage unknown against sector medians.

The recent Permian acquisitions and the enlarged repurchase authorization absorb capital and raise the bar for cash-flow durability; the post-year-end divestiture proceeds reduced borrowings, which we view favourably, but the equity-funded growth strategy keeps the credit sensitive to operator concentration and commodity prices.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流覆蓋宣派股息超過三倍，因此基礎分派由內部產生現金而非借款支付，對一項並無資本開支承擔的特許權業務而言，這是具意義的緩衝。
流動比率遠高於行業中位數，反映在溫和的短期負債下具備流動的營運資金狀況；儘管該比率因流動負債基數偏低而被美化，仍支持短期債務的履行。

key_risks.text: 特許權收入集中：兩家營運商各自貢獻超過一成收入，而發行人並無向購買方取得抵押品，因此營運商無力償債或付款違約將直接打擊現金流，且無抵銷性擔保。
循環融資及定期貸款項下借款按 term SOFR 加差價浮動，令利息成本暴露於利率重設；定期貸款僅於年結後以出售資產所得償還，因此再融資及利率風險延續至本期。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運收入為負而已付現金利息仍屬重大，因此呈報的利息覆蓋率為負且遠低於行業中位數；以盈利為基礎的債務償付因此未獲體現，現金流必須承擔此負擔。
現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數但高於下一風險區間界線，餘裕有限；營運現金流溫和下降將令該比率推向較低層級，因此分派政策及商品價格值得密切監察。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為溫和，以強勁現金轉換及流動資產負債表為錨，但槓桿無法評估，因資料包內並無披露折舊及資本開支，令總槓桿及淨槓桿相對於行業中位數屬未知。
近期二疊紀盆地收購及擴大後的回購授權吸納資本並提高現金流持久性的門檻；年結後出售資產所得減少借款，我們對此持正面看法，但以股本集資的增長策略令信貸對營運商集中度及商品價格保持敏感。
